name: Chronic Intestinal Pseudo-Obstruction (Secondary Forms)

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic Criteria for Chronic Intestinal Pseudo-Obstruction

criteria.description: Recurrent symptoms of intestinal obstruction without mechanical cause
Imaging showing dilated bowel loops with air-fluid levels without mechanical obstruction
Abnormal intestinal motility demonstrated by manometry
Identification of underlying systemic or metabolic disorder causing dysmotility

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of recurrent obstructive symptoms without mechanical cause plus radiologic evidence and abnormal motility studies
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Exclusion of mechanical obstruction is mandatory; secondary causes must be investigated.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Severe abdominal distension without mechanical obstruction

common.symptomName: Weight loss due to malabsorption or poor intake

rare.symptomName: Signs of sepsis secondary to bacterial overgrowth
Peripheral neuropathy (if related to underlying systemic disease)

laboratory: Markers of underlying systemic disease (e.g., autoimmune markers)
imaging: Abdominal X-ray showing dilated bowel loops with air-fluid levels
genetic: No primary genetic mutations; secondary forms associated with systemic diseases
other: Manometry showing abnormal intestinal motility patterns
Histopathology may show neuropathic or myopathic changes in intestinal wall

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of anatomical obstruction on imaging or surgery
Often presents in childhood or young adulthood

redFlags: Signs of bowel ischemia or perforation
references: Camilleri M, et al. Chronic Intestinal Pseudo-Obstruction: Diagnosis and Management. Gastroenterology. 2020.
Knowles CH, et al. Chronic Intestinal Pseudo-Obstruction: Clinical Features and Management. Nat Rev Gastroenterol Hepatol. 2013.
Orphanet: Chronic Intestinal Pseudo-Obstruction Secondary Forms. 2024.
